headline: Myanmar's president visits Malaysia amid protests

sources.title: Myanmar's military-backed leader turns to diplomacy on Malaysia visit (AP News)
Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing visits Malaysia amid concerns over repatriations (Al Jazeera)
Malaysia to work towards Myanmar's full reintegration into ASEAN, PM says (The Jakarta Post)
Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing and Malaysia PM Anwar to meet tomorrow; repatriation talks top agenda (video, CNA)

chunks.text: On October 7, 2026, Myanmar's president arrived in Malaysia for a [[two-day visit]]. It was his first trip there since he became president in April. As [[army chief]], he led the military when it {{took over}} the country in 2021. That move started a [[civil war]]. Relations with the region {{broke down}} after that. Since April, his government has been {{reaching out}} to nearby countries to [[restore]] [[ties]].

verbs.correct: To take control of something by force
verbs.wrong: To hold an election for a new leader
verbs.why: The army took over the country and closed the airports. Rebels took over the city in a single night. The military took over Myanmar in 2021, when the president was the army chief.

verbs.correct: To fail and come to an end
verbs.why: Their marriage broke down after years of fighting. Talks between the two companies broke down in May. Relations between Myanmar and most of the region broke down after 2021.

verbs.correct: To try to make contact with others
verbs.wrong: To send soldiers to a border
verbs.why: The new mayor is reaching out to local business owners. Our school reached out to parents about the new rules. Myanmar's government has been reaching out to its neighbors in Southeast Asia.

chunks.text: Since 2021, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations has {{shut Myanmar's leaders out}} of its top meetings. The trip was his fifth to a member of this [[regional bloc]]. On October 8, he met Malaysia's prime minister. The prime minister said [[trade]] between them {{went up}} by more than 140 percent in a year. He said Malaysia would do whatever it could to bring Myanmar back into the bloc.

verbs.correct: To not allow someone to take part
verbs.wrong: To ask someone to lead a meeting
verbs.why: The older kids shut him out of their game. The company shut small shops out of the deal. The regional bloc has shut Myanmar's leaders out of its top meetings since 2021.
The price of eggs went up again. Our rent goes up every January. Trade between Malaysia and Myanmar went up by more than 140 percent in a year.

chunks.text: After he landed, the president tried to {{win over}} Malaysian [[investors]]. He told them Myanmar was on a [[path toward democracy]], state television reported. Malaysia said the invitation was not a formal [[recognition]] of his government. [[Rights groups]] say the general election was designed to help the military {{hold on to}} power. On October 8, a few dozen people {{showed up}} for a [[protest]] inside a building in the capital. An activist said the region should not give him [[legitimacy]].

verbs.correct: To get someone to support you
verbs.why: The coach worked hard to win over the new players. She won over the voters with her plan for schools. The president tried to win over Malaysian investors after he landed.

verbs.correct: To keep control and not lose it
verbs.wrong: To build new roads and schools
verbs.why: The party wants to hold on to power after the next vote. The old king held on to power for forty years. Rights groups say the general election was designed to help the military hold on to power.

verbs.correct: To attend an event or meeting
verbs.wrong: To vote in a local election
verbs.why: Only ten people showed up for the meeting. More fans showed up than the stadium could hold. A few dozen people showed up for a protest against the visit in Malaysia's capital.

chunks.text: Malaysia says it has {{sent back}} 10,493 Myanmar citizens since January 2026. Nearly 1,500 of them went home in late September. The United Nations refugee agency and rights groups have {{spoken out}} against the returns. They warn that people could face [[persecution]] and [[forced military service]] in a [[war zone]]. The prime minister has {{pushed back}}. He says Malaysia cannot host [[undocumented]] foreigners forever. The president promised to {{speed up}} the returns. Another 11,804 remain in Malaysian [[detention centers]].

verbs.correct: To return someone to their country
verbs.wrong: To teach someone a new language
verbs.why: The border guards sent the travelers back because they had no visas. Officials sent him back to his home country after his visa ended. Malaysia says it has sent back 10,493 Myanmar citizens since January 2026.

verbs.correct: To say publicly that something is wrong
verbs.wrong: To check facts before a report
verbs.why: Several doctors have spoken out against the new health law. She spoke out about unsafe working conditions at the factory. Rights groups have spoken out against Malaysia's returns of Myanmar nationals.

verbs.correct: To resist an idea or criticism
verbs.wrong: To count votes after an election
verbs.why: Teachers pushed back against the longer school day. When people criticized the plan, the mayor pushed back. Malaysia's prime minister has pushed back against criticism of the returns.
The city wants to speed up repairs on the bridge. A new machine will speed up the work at the factory. Myanmar's president promised to speed up the returns from Malaysia.

mainIdea.s: Myanmar's president made a two-day trip to Malaysia to rebuild ties after his country was shut out of top regional meetings. The visit drew praise from Malaysia's leader but also protests.
mainIdea.why: The president has been reaching out to Southeast Asia after relations broke down in 2021. Some people showed up to protest the visit.

mainIdea.s: Malaysia agreed to stop sending Myanmar nationals home after a meeting with Myanmar's leader. In return, he promised his country would hold a new election and free all political prisoners.
mainIdea.why: Close, but Malaysia has not stopped the returns. It has sent back 10,493 people, and the president promised to speed up the process.

mainIdea.s: Leaders from across Southeast Asia met in Bangkok to plan help for flood victims in northern Myanmar. They agreed to send food, medicine and engineers to the worst affected villages quickly.
mainIdea.why: Myanmar's president visited Malaysia, not Bangkok. He tried to win over investors and talked about returns of Myanmar nationals.

tf.s: Rights groups have spoken out against Malaysia's returns of Myanmar nationals.
tf.why: The United Nations refugee agency and rights groups warn that returnees could face persecution and forced military service.

tf.s: Malaysia said its invitation formally recognized the president's government.
tf.why: Malaysia said the invitation was not a formal recognition of his government. A small group of people showed up to protest the visit.

tf.s: Malaysia has sent back thousands of Myanmar citizens to their home country.
tf.why: Malaysia says it has sent back more than 10,000 people since January 2026, and more remain in detention centers.

tf.s: The president refused to speed up the returns from Malaysia.
tf.why: He promised to speed up the returns. Still, 11,804 Myanmar nationals remain in detention centers in Malaysia.

tf.s: Trade between the two countries went up by more than 140 percent in a year.
tf.why: Malaysia's prime minister said trade went up by that much when he met Myanmar's president.

tf.s: The regional bloc invites Myanmar's leaders to all of its top meetings.
tf.why: Since 2021, the bloc has shut Myanmar's leaders out of its top meetings.

lines.text: Did you see that Myanmar's president went to Malaysia?
I did. Isn't he the general whose army {{took over}} in 2021?
That's him. Now he's president, and he's {{reaching out}} to the region.
Why does he need to do that?
Relations {{broke down}} after 2021. The regional bloc {{shut his country's leaders out}} of its top meetings.
So Malaysia gave him the [[red carpet treatment]]?
Pretty much. There was an honor guard, and the prime minister said trade {{went up}} a lot.
He also tried to {{win over}} investors, right?
Yes. But with a civil war in the country, that's [[a tough sell]].
A few dozen people {{showed up}}. Rights groups say the election just helped the military {{hold on to}} power.
And what about the people Malaysia has {{sent back}}?
That's the big issue. The UN refugee agency has {{spoken out}} about the dangers.
But the prime minister {{pushed back}}, didn't he?
He did. He says Malaysia can't host undocumented people forever. He's [[between a rock and a hard place]].
I have [[mixed feelings]] about the whole thing.
Me too. The president even promised to {{speed up}} the returns.
Well, it's [[a balancing act]] for Malaysia. Both sides want something.

expressions.def: Used to say that someone is welcomed in a very special and formal way
ex: The famous actor got the red carpet treatment at the hotel.
The team received the red carpet treatment when it returned home.

expressions.def: Used to say that something is hard to get people to accept
ex: A longer school day will be a tough sell with students.

expressions.expr: between a rock and a hard place
expressions.def: Used to say that someone must choose between two bad options
ex: With no money and no job offers, she was between a rock and a hard place.

expressions.def: Used to say that you feel both good and bad about something
ex: I have mixed feelings about moving to a new city.
He had mixed feelings when his team won by cheating.

expressions.def: Used to describe a situation where you must try to meet two different needs
ex: Working and going to school at the same time is a balancing act.
Running a family budget is a balancing act.
